qs.q: A researcher measures basal metabolic rate in a patient undergoing starvation. Which hormonal shift primarily sustains blood glucose levels during prolonged fasting states?
qs.e: Glucagon secretion increases during fasting to stimulate hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, maintaining glycemia.

qs.q: A clinical dietitian is analyzing the physiological predisposing factors for adult obesity in a patient. Which factor is directly associated with a reduced basal metabolic rate that promotes weight gain?
qs.e: Low thyroxine levels reduce the basal metabolic rate (BMR), predisposing individuals to weight gain and obesity. High sodium causes fluid retention and hypertension rather than lowering baseline energy expenditure.

exam: A 28‑year‑old woman with weight loss, heat intolerance and tachycardia presents; what bedside test helps differentiate thyroid storm from simple hyperthyroidism? — Look for fever > 40 °C, altered mental status, and heart failure; these indicate thyroid storm.

A malnourished HIV‑positive man has persistent hypothermia; which hormone assay is most informative? — Serum TSH and free T₄; a high TSH with low free T₄ points to hypothyroidism contributing to low BMR.

In a patient with unexplained fever, you cannot obtain indirect calorimetry; how do you estimate energy needs? — Use the Harris‑Benedict equation adjusted for weight and activity, then add 10‑20 % for fever.
Why is propranolol preferred over atenolol in hyperthyroid patients? — Propranolol blocks β‑adrenergic effects and also reduces peripheral conversion of T₄ to T₃; atenolol lacks the latter effect.

A pregnant woman in her second trimester reports increased appetite but no weight gain; what physiologic change explains this? — BMR rises 15‑20 % in the second and third trimester, increasing calorie needs by ~300 kcal/day.
How does iodine deficiency affect BMR in a rural East African community? — Low iodine impairs thyroid hormone synthesis, leading to reduced BMR, cold intolerance, and growth retardation.
A patient on amiodarone develops bradycardia and weight gain; what is the likely mechanism? — Amiodine‑induced hypothyroidism reduces thyroid hormone levels, lowering BMR and slowing cardiac rate.

What feature distinguishes hypothyroid myopathy from malnutrition‑related muscle wasting? — Hypothyroid myopathy shows slowed reflex relaxation and elevated CK, whereas malnutrition shows normal reflexes and low albumin.
ai.title: Basal Metabolic Rate
ai.subject: Biochemistry & genetics
ai.summary: Basal metabolic rate (BMR) is the energy needed to maintain vital functions at rest. Thyroid hormones are the main regulators, and alterations affect temperature, cardiac output and nutrition. Understanding BMR helps explain weight changes, fever, and critical illness in low‑resource settings.

b: Measured in kcal·day⁻¹ or mL O₂·min⁻¹
Higher in men, infants, and those with more lean mass
sections.p: BMR is the amount of oxygen consumed (or calories burned) per minute by a person at complete rest, in a thermoneutral environment, after an overnight fast. It accounts for ~60‑70 % of total daily energy expenditure.

b: T₃ binds nuclear receptors → ↑ transcription of metabolic enzymes
↑ β‑adrenergic receptor density amplifies catecholamine effects
sections.p: Cellular metabolism uses ATP generated by oxidative phosphorylation. Thyroid hormones (T₃, T₄) increase Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase activity, uncoupling protein expression, and mitochondrial oxidative capacity, raising oxygen consumption.
The hypothalamic‑pituitary‑thyroid axis sets thyroid hormone output. Peripheral conversion of T₄ to T₃ in liver, kidney and muscle fine‑tunes BMR. Illness, malnutrition and drugs can blunt this axis.

b: Hyperthyroidism: ↑ BMR, heat intolerance, weight loss, tachycardia
Hypothyroidism: ↓ BMR, cold intolerance, weight gain, bradycardia
sections.p: Disorders that raise or lower thyroid hormone alter BMR, producing characteristic clinical patterns.

b: Unexplained weight loss → check for hyperthyroidism, TB, HIV
Persistent hypothermia in a septic patient → consider hypothyroidism
sections.p: In low‑resource hospitals, BMR changes guide assessment of fever, malnutrition, and drug toxicity. Recognising a deranged BMR prevents mis‑attribution of weight loss to infection alone.

t.b: Is the thyroid axis suppressed or over‑active? Low TSH with high free T₄ confirms primary hyperthyroidism; high TSH with low free T₄ confirms primary hypothyroidism.
Provides objective BMR measurement; if unavailable, use predictive equations (e.g., Harris‑Benedict) adjusted for weight and height.
